title: MMSBUILD delivery board
note: Modules are the PRD's phases, tasks are its requirements, subtasks are its acceptance criteria. Ids match the PRD exactly, so an acceptance run maps to this board line for line. `status` is ours — what is built. `verified` belongs to the acceptance run and is never set by us.

status.doing: In progress — work still to do here
status.awaiting-owner: Finished here. Waiting on an action only the owner can take, named in the note.
status.blocked: Cannot proceed — something named in `blockedBy` has to be solved first

verified.pending: Not yet run by the other party

modules.title: Phase 0 — Close the surface
modules.summary: Every requirement after this one assumes an authenticated admin.

tasks.title: Admin authentication
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: every admin route on the control plane and every console page requires a signed-in administrator — scrypt password, a signed 12-hour session scoped to the console, per-email lockout after repeated failures. One check sits ahead of every route, and a self-test fails if an admin route is ever left outside it. The connector keeps site creation only, on its own token. The board is no longer served on the public address. Live since 2026-09-17: on the public address every admin route answers 401 without a session, the console redirects to sign-in, and the public board path is gone.

subtasks.text: Unauthenticated admin request refused; the console requires sign-in

tasks.title: The admin surface reveals no secret it does not have to
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: machine keys are stored as a hash only, the read-back route is gone, and stored copies are wiped at startup. The project listing carries no invite link, no AI gateway token and no secret-bearing field; a new invite link is shown once, when issued. Links already shared keep working until used or replaced. Live since 2026-09-17: a signed-in project listing carries no invite link, token or secret-bearing field, and a key read-back answers 404.

subtasks.text: A minted machine key cannot be read back in plaintext
A project listing leaks no usable invite link or capacity token

modules.title: Phase 1 — The levels
modules.summary: Operator and Business above Project, with roles that hold when the interface is bypassed.

tasks.title: Operator and Business levels above Project
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: Operators own Businesses, Businesses own projects, and a Business with no Operator sits directly under the platform. Every stored record carries its Operator and Business, stamped by the database, so moving a project or a Business re-addresses everything under it. Console accounts are scoped to the platform, one Operator or one Business; every read and change is limited to that scope, and a project outside it answers "not found". The chain is listed in the console's Organisation page and by the organisation API. The existing projects each became a Business of their own; the staging copy shares its site's. Project processes now hold only their own signing key and no control-plane credentials, so a project cannot reach another Business through its own server either. Builder smoke test 2026-09-17: an Operator and a Business under it were created in the console. The console was then redesigned to match the MMS-CMS — the shared MMS header, pages in setup order (Organisation → Projects → People → Access), dialogs for every create and change, confirmations for destructive actions, and themed dropdowns. Builder check 2026-09-18: the redesigned console was confirmed working. Two faults found in that check are fixed — a dropdown inside a dialog drew its options behind the dialog, so they were invisible, and the console was being served in development mode, which made every page fetch its source file by file. The console now runs from its build and each page asks the control plane for everything it needs at once: pages that took 1–2 seconds now answer in 15–30 ms.

subtasks.text: The Operator → Business → Project chain is queryable; each level resolves its children
Cross-Business read and write denied at the server; no foreign data in any listing

tasks.title: Roles, and more than one person per project
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: a project has any number of people, each with one of the CMS's own four roles — Owner, Publisher (the CMS admin role), Author (the CMS client role: edits content, cannot publish) and Viewer. People are invited, re-roled and removed from the console's People page. The CMS enforces the role on every request, so a denial holds for a direct call as well as in the interface. A role change or removal reaches the CMS at once, including for a session that is already open. Live since the 2026-09-17 restart.

subtasks.text: Publisher-role action allowed; the same action denied to an author role
The denial holds when the interface is bypassed

tasks.title: Inviting a second person must not overwrite the first
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: an invite adds an account. Re-inviting someone who already has access is refused instead of locking them out; re-inviting someone still invited only replaces their link. When one email belongs to several projects, sign-in asks which project rather than picking one. Live since the 2026-09-17 restart.

subtasks.text: A second invite adds an account rather than replacing the first

tasks.title: A portal sign-in arrives with its own role, not as the owner
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-17: the hub's signed hand-off names the person and their role; the CMS signs them in as their own account with that role, and the design studio records who is working. Step-up is never pre-satisfied: it asks for the person's hub password, checked by the control plane, and an unreachable check fails. Sessions that the old hand-off opened with step-up already satisfied are ended at upgrade. The design studio's Share to CMS now brings the person into the CMS as themselves. Only the agent gateway and the studio's own server-side staging use a machine sign-in, which the hub never issues. Live since the 2026-09-17 daemon rebuild and restart.

subtasks.text: An author role is denied an owner-only action inside the CMS
Step-up is demanded, not pre-satisfied

modules.title: Phase 2 — Scoped visibility and branding
modules.summary: Counts without the work, and an Operator's own branding.

tasks.title: Platform Owner sees counts, not work; Operators are branded
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-18: the Platform Owner sees counts and status across the estate and opens no project by default. Four ways in were closed — minting an agent key, installing the bridge, inviting yourself to a project, and the unlinked route that put a project on a public address — and listing MCP keys no longer opens an owner session inside every project on each page load. Opening a business’s work is now "Act as this business": it asks why, records the answer before anything is handed over, puts platform staff on that project’s People list under their own name so the customer can see them, and ends after an hour or on exit — which removes the person, and so revokes the session in MMS-CMS and MMS-Design as well as the hub. Every administrator action is now recorded with the actor and, where it applies, who they were acting as; the trail is read on a new Activity page, scoped like everything else. Branding is per-Operator: logo, name and accent colour, set by upload or by pasting an address (fetched once and stored, so an agency’s customers never call a third-party server). It reaches the hub pages, both products’ headers, their browser tab titles and icons, and the console — with no per-Operator build, because the gateway answers the icon addresses the built pages already ask for and rewrites the title in the document it is already touching. A Business directly under the platform keeps MMSBUILD’s. The PRD’s AC-A5.2 referred to a list of "branded surfaces" that did not exist; it is authored in the PRD now (S1–S8).

subtasks.text: Counts visible to the platform-owner role; opening the work denied
Operator branding renders on the named surfaces

modules.title: Phase 3 — One project, one website
modules.summary: A second design can never silently destroy the first.

tasks.title: A second website cannot silently destroy the first

subtasks.text: A second design is refused or lands distinctly; site A still resolves with A's content

tasks.note: Built 2026-09-18: a share now says which design it is carrying, and a website records the design it was built from — until now the handover was files and nothing else, so "this design again" and "a different design" arrived down one path looking identical. That is what destroyed the first website: the wizard empties the site before it plans the import, which is exactly why no conflict was ever detected and why the result read as a successful update. A different design into a project with a published website is now refused, before anything is staged, with a message naming how many pages are there and which design built them. A different design over unpublished work is not refused — iterating before launch is normal — but the wizard stops and names what would go, and nothing is touched until the person agrees. Re-sharing the SAME design still overwrites in place, unchanged: "no duplicates on re-share" depends on it, and it is the thing most easily broken by fixing the rest. The PRD referred to "a different design" and to "already has a website" without defining either; both are defined in the PRD now.

tasks.title: The CMS destination belongs to the project

subtasks.text: A design's destination cannot be pointed at another project's CMS
Publishing to A changes A's domain and not B's, verified by fetching both

tasks.note: Built 2026-09-18: nothing ever chose the wrong CMS — the destination is one value per design-studio process, with no parameter, setting or screen — but nothing checked either: a mis-aimed push failed only because the receiving project’s key would reject the token, an accident rather than a rule. The CMS now refuses a hand-off that does not name it, and refuses one when it does not know which project it is, rather than accepting anything. The destination is also always stated rather than inherited, so a stray value in the control plane’s environment can no longer become a lite project’s CMS. On the domain side, the Cloudflare project and the custom domain were free text with no uniqueness rule, so two projects could name one destination — a typo, or a -staging clone keeping its source’s — and publishing either would have uploaded onto the other’s live domain; the database now refuses it and the console says which project already holds it. Separately, the design studio kept its Cloudflare credentials in a directory shared by every project on the host, letting any project’s studio attach any domain in that account; each project now keeps its own, and MMS-CMS stays the sole publisher (PRD §5.1).

tasks.title: Per-property approver: registration, delegation, rotation

Rotation retires the old row and inserts the new one in a single batch, so a property is never left with two live identities or none by accident, and the retired identity stops being accepted immediately rather than at the next restart — with history kept so an old receipt can still be explained. Revocation without a replacement leaves the property refusing everything. Delegation is explicit: a business-level approver reaches only the properties its registration names, never what a hierarchy implies. And the fallback is gone: a property with no registered approver is refused rather than handed to the platform-wide key that, until this change, approved every site on the estate — "a fallback that widens scope on error is a master key by another name". tasks.title: Import and publish each gated, bound, and gated separately
tasks.note: Completed 2026-09-21: the exemption list is removed from the policy, the loader and the gate. A staging project is now gated exactly like a production one, because "a staging project exempted from the approval gate proves nothing" — the loop being rehearsed has to be the real one. The type that carried the gate result can no longer express "passed without an approval" at all, so the exemption cannot be reintroduced by configuration. NOTE 2026-09-21: the gate itself runs here and refuses correctly, but granting an approval needs the approver registry, which is not deployed (see R6). So the refusal half is provable today and the success half — AC-B7.5, import and publish under separate approvals — is not, until the relay is redeployed.

B7.1–B7.4 still refused when the caller holds valid machine credentials

tasks.title: Fail-closed everywhere
tasks.note: Completed 2026-09-21: the share’s compliance check no longer fails open. It used to pre-seed the outgoing files with the unchecked input and swallow any error into a warning, so a crash in the checker produced an HTTP 200 with a redirect — byte-identical to a clean pass — and staged the unchecked site. The verdict had no way to say "could not check": it now does, per page, so one unparseable page cannot destroy the verdict on the others. A crash and an unjudged page both block, under their own error code, distinguishable from a compliance failure and from success. Separately the model-capability check, which deliberately allowed a save through when the catalogue could not be read, now refuses — that was a check reporting a pass because it could not run, which principle P2 forbids in writing.

subtasks.text: A crashed importability check blocks, distinguishably from a success
Missing or unreadable policy: every gated action refuses
A check that cannot run yields failure, never a zero-findings pass

tasks.title: The proof chain: receipt, live verification, known-good, immutability
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-21: the publish now says what it published. The content hash was computed to check If-Match and then discarded, and the deploy webhook carried no body, so nothing about WHAT went live ever reached the side that recorded the deploy — which is why a receipt could name a time and a URL and nothing else. Receipts are a new append-only table whose triggers refuse any later edit or delete, carrying the content identity, the page count, the Cloudflare project and deployment id, the verification result, the previous receipt, the retained bundle and the build that did it. "Live" is no longer a regex over the deploy tool’s output: the site is fetched afterwards and each sampled route must serve ITS OWN page, so a host answering its fallback under a 200 is caught — an HTTP-200 check is explicitly not sufficient. A check that cannot run reports "unverified", never success. The bundle that was uploaded is copied out after the deploy writes its root files, because the CMS keeps two generations and destroys the older one as the first step of the next publish, so there was no spare generation to point at.

subtasks.text: A receipt per publish with every named field present
Verification fetches the site; a missing route serving a fallback is caught as FAIL
A known-good bundle is retained and reconstructs the prior state
Editing or deleting a past receipt is denied

tasks.title: The two ends do not trust each other
tasks.note: Held and reinforced 2026-09-21: the two implementations still share no code. The shared vectors covered only single-key signature checks, so per-property resolution was asserted twice in two suites that share nothing — the moment R6 landed, the two resolvers could have drifted with all nine signature cases still green. The vectors now carry nine resolution cases as well (own approver, unregistered property, empty registry, delegation covering and not covering, project winning over business, an unusable key, a retired approver), and both sides run them against their own resolver.

subtasks.text: Verification succeeds with the issuing side offline, using unshared code
A tampered approval fails on the acting side; both sides pass the shared suite

modules.title: Phase 5 — The repeatable push
modules.summary: A new site pushed with zero developer round trips.

tasks.title: Pre-flight is the gate
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-21: the pre-flight is now a decision, not a report. It carries `ok` and coded findings alongside the sentences it always had, and a blocking finding refuses the import before anything reaches the CMS. Gating one call site was not enough — four paths could land a bundle, and two of them (archive and draft import) computed nothing at all; every path now projects, and the publish path gates too, against the draft as the CMS actually holds it, so a site that would bake broken is caught however its content arrived — bundle import, draft import, or a person editing in the admin. A check that could not run refuses rather than passing. There is no override. Two real bugs surfaced on the way: the projection compared rule ids against rule names, which made both "kept for" lists silently empty for every real bundle (the fixture set name === id, so the suite agreed with itself); and it predicted routes the bake provably never writes — template pages, unpublished rows, and rows of a table with no entry template. The threshold stays at a quarter, deliberately: PRD 5.5 warns against calibrating it against the wrong build, so v4 (8 of 617) and v7 (600 of 666) are both pinned as fixtures — the first must block, the second must pass.

subtasks.text: A known-broken bundle is reported and blocked before import
Surviving-rule count, dropped rules, routes and what-is-missing, all parseable
Predicted routes equal published routes
subtasks.note: Prediction and bake now share one implementation of a site's URL shape rather than two that were free to drift, and the publish reports the routes it actually baked, so the prediction is compared against reality instead of against itself.

tasks.title: Fonts: idempotent install, and survival across a replace
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-21: a replace no longer loses the fonts the new design still uses. The design blank stays — it is what stops a re-share accumulating stale fonts from previous shares — but the registry is now reconciled across it rather than simply dropped: a family the incoming design actually references comes back, and one it no longer uses does not. References are read from style rules, from breakpoint variants, and from raw stylesheets, which is where a hand-written design keeps its typography. Tokens return only when their family does, since a token pointing at a missing family resolves to a bare fallback stack — the unstyled result the whole requirement is about. The font files were never deleted by any of this, so what was lost was metadata and what is restored points at bytes that are still there.

subtasks.text: Font install returns ids; re-running changes nothing
Intended fonts render on the live page after a replace-style import
subtasks.note: connector_list_fonts reports installed families and what each token resolves to, so "the font survived the replace" is something a machine can assert instead of something somebody looks at.

tasks.title: Per-page SEO renders unconditionally
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-21: better than this board said, and now complete. Title, description, canonical, Open Graph and JSON-LD were already emitted by the core publisher on the only public render path, with no capability check and no plugin — there is no SEO plugin in the repo at all. What was missing was the schema: five of the seven fields had to be added per project by a connector call, so a site that skipped the step emitted no canonical tag. They are part of the stock pages and posts schema now, for new projects and existing ones alike, and the field names match what the renderer already reads.

subtasks.text: Milestone — a new site pushed with zero developer round trips
subtasks.note: Asserted as arithmetic rather than description: the test records who acted, and the milestone is the assertion that the developer list is empty while the owner signed exactly twice.
blockedBy: the owner signing the two GOs a first push needs

tasks.note: Built 2026-09-21. One operation runs the whole sequence PRD 5.4 names — pre-flight, import under the owner-signed GO, inspect, publish under a second GO — and it drives the ordinary import and publish tools rather than reimplementing them, so it passes exactly the gates a person would. An orchestrator that called the CMS directly would be a way around those gates, which is the same as not having them. It never blocks on a person: each call advances as far as it can and reports whose move it is, state lives on disk so the wait outlives the process, and the relay's own replay means a resumed step reuses the ticket it already opened instead of putting a second deploy-request in front of the owner. A parked run resumes by itself once the signature exists — by polling, because the relay is a Worker and the Connector listens on loopback behind the gateway, so the webhook that looks more elegant is the one that cannot be delivered. A bundle the pre-flight refuses stops the run BEFORE anyone is asked to approve it. Two things outside the loop were what actually kept the count above zero, and both are fixed: the stack's own launcher read its credentials from whatever shell happened to start it rather than from platform configuration — the literal reading of "without a developer holding the credentials" — and a service that exited stayed dead until somebody noticed, which is a developer round trip by any measure. Services now restart with backoff, and configuration comes from the platform's own file. Project creation also says plainly that a new project has no approver and how the owner registers one, instead of letting a first push fail at its first approval with a message about a registry nobody mentioned. ONE THING DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the studio's Share-to-CMS path still ends at a browser wizard. That is a decision on record, not an omission — the browser runs the same wizard a manual drag-drop uses, so Share to CMS cannot drift from manual import, and a server-side adapter would be a second implementation of the importer. It costs no DEVELOPER action, which is what this requirement counts; the studio operating its own tool is the studio doing its job. PENDING, and this status was wrong before: it was set to built while the live relay still answered "No such route" for the registry the loop depends on. The loop opens deploy-requests and reads GOs on that relay, so until it is redeployed the push cannot run against production at all — everything asserted above is asserted against tests and a local stack. It moves to built when the owner has deployed and a real push has been run end to end. STATUS, corrected again: "blocked" overstated it — nothing here is stuck. The loop is written, committed and passing; what it waits on is the relay redeploy, which needs a Cloudflare login the owner holds and we do not, and an approver registered for whatever project it pushes to (see R6). It moves to built when both are true and a real push has run end to end. LIVE 2026-09-24. The owner deployed relay 0.5.1 and applied the migration. Verified from outside, by us: /api/health reports 0.5.1 and points at /api/health/approvers; the registry lists sheeltron-staging at project level; POST /api/approvers anonymously answers 302 (Access login) rather than 403, which is the closed state — a 403 there would mean the path had been bypassed and the write door left open. The Connector was restarted and its own resolver now reads the live registry: sheeltron-staging resolves at property scope, while "sheeltron" and an unregistered property are both REFUSED — the no-platform-fallback rule holding against the real service, not a fixture. So both of R13's blockers are now cleared — the relay is deployed AND sheeltron-staging has an approver. It stays awaiting-owner rather than moving to built for an honest reason: the push has never been exercised end to end against a live relay, and "the blocker is gone" is not the same claim as "it works". A first run can be started whenever the owner is ready to sign; it parks at the gate by design and resumes by itself once the signature exists, so the wait costs nothing. Note the criterion counts DEVELOPER actions and round-trips at zero — the owner signing is part of the loop, not a violation of it.
blockedBy: the owner signing the two GOs a first push needs (import, then publish)

modules.title: Phase 6 — Productionisation
modules.summary: Safe replace, complete clear-all, and an honest cold start.

tasks.title: Safe replace, and a complete clear-all
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-22. AC-D15.2 was already satisfied by the clear-all, which covers all four stores in the right order with the tenant stopped first. AC-D15.1 was unmet on BOTH halves and the board understated it: the replace path took no backup at all, and the one backup that existed — the clear-all's — had no reader anywhere in the repository AND omitted `data_row_versions` and `site_snapshots`, which is precisely the published state this requirement is about. It could not have satisfied the criterion even if something had read it. A replace now captures the published state before destroying it — rows, versions, snapshots, custom table definitions and redirects — and a restore writes it back in one transaction, in FK order, with the active-version pointer applied in a second pass because a single-pass insert cannot satisfy a cycle. A page comes back PUBLISHED, not merely present, which is the whole difference. The format carries a version and a checksum and the reader refuses anything it does not fully understand, including every backup written before today: half-applying one over a live site is worse than refusing it. A backup that fails stops the import, because a replace with no backup is the exact outcome the requirement exists to prevent. Three generations are kept, the number R9 already chose for known-good bundles. A replace also now clears the `site_snapshots` it used to orphan — nothing in the server had ever deleted them. NOT DONE, deliberately: a replace still leaves the baked `published/` files serving. The clear-all deletes them because it is a deliberate wipe; for an import, keeping the old pages up until the next publish is what avoids taking a live site down between the two steps. ALSO NOT DONE: the clear-all script still writes the old backup format, so its backups remain unrestorable. Its own criterion (AC-D15.2) does not depend on that, and it is named here rather than left to be rediscovered.

subtasks.text: Prior published state recoverable after a replace
A deleted page stays gone from every store after clear-all

tasks.title: Cold-start clarity
tasks.note: Built 2026-09-22, and the defect was worse than this note said. The console did not merely confuse "not up yet" with "not installed" — it had NO studio status at all. It rendered the CMS runtime for every project, so a design-only project read "Stopped" with a "Start" button permanently, whatever the studio was doing. Nor could the underlying check have helped: the one the listing called is true from the instant spawn() returns and stays true for the whole multi-minute boot. The honest predicate existed and was never called from the listing. The studio now reports four states that are genuinely different things — not provisioned, starting, ready, failed with its reason — and the console shows the studio separately from the CMS, because they have separate lifecycles and folding them together is what caused this. A start time is recorded, which nothing tracked before, so "starting" can be told from "stuck": the chip says how long. "Start" is no longer offered for a studio that is already starting, and the page keeps looking while anything is coming up — it used to refresh only during provisioning, so a cold start never resolved on screen. All of it reads in-process state and probes nothing: probing each project on a listing once opened an owner session inside every one, which R5 forbids and a self-test guards. ADJACENT, not fixed: the bridge-plugin chip has an identical bug, turning "the CMS is unreachable" into "not installed". It is not AC-D16.1 and was not bundled in.

subtasks.text: A cold studio returns "starting", not something that reads as "not installed"

modules.title: Security acceptance — the locked ten
modules.summary: Run by someone other than the builder, on a throwaway or staging project, never on a live site. CORRECTED 2026-09-23: this used to say five have no control at all. That was wrong for E2, E7 and E8 — each already had real, enforced, server-side controls. Checking that claim turned up six genuine defects, which are now fixed; what is mostly outstanding is PROOF, not mechanism.

tasks.title: Secret access blocked

subtasks.text: Covered by NEW-1a / NEW-1b

tasks.title: Network and tool allowlists enforced
tasks.note: NOTE CORRECTED 2026-09-23 — "no test and no control" was false. Four enforced, fail-closed allowlists already existed: per-run tool endpoints (tool-tokens.ts, 403 on an undeclared endpoint), connector tool names (service.ts, re-checked at execution), CMS capability-gated tools (capabilityGate.ts, re-checked at dispatch) and the browser network guard (browser-network-policy.ts), which also already had a test. THREE REAL GAPS FOUND AND FIXED: the reasoning-egress policy was supplied by the CALLER, so an omitted field meant unrestricted — it is now server-owned and a caller may only narrow it; the AI gateway forwarded any upstream path verbatim, so a tenant chose which endpoint the operator's key paid for — now allowlisted; and a body declaring JSON that failed to parse was forwarded UNPINNED, skipping model enforcement — now refused. Also pinned: the connector allowlist grew itself from provider-supplied tool names and descriptions; that widening is now opt-in and off by default. STILL OPEN: OD_SANDBOX_MODE is set nowhere outside the test suite, so the import-containment control is fully implemented, covered by ten test files, and has never once executed in production. Enabling it changes every tenant daemon's runtime and is deliberately last. Acceptance runbook not written.

subtasks.text: Controls exist and three fail-opens are fixed; sandbox mode not yet enabled; runbook outstanding

tasks.title: Prompt-injection attempts rejected
tasks.note: PARTLY BUILT 2026-09-23. The board said "no test and no control" — true, and the injection surface turned out to be concrete rather than theoretical. The content agent interpolated CMS row values RAW into the SYSTEM prompt (title, every field value, collection slugs), and the content scope skipped the snapshot validation the site scope does — a bare cast over the untrusted HTTP body. "The tenant wrote that row" is not generally true: rows arrive from third-party HTML imports, from the Connector (one bearer token, whole tool surface) and from caller-chosen media filenames, which content_list_media handed straight to the model. DONE: the snapshot is now validated; stored content is fenced and marked as data wherever it reaches a prompt, with the value unable to close its own fence; and the rule explaining the fence sits in the static prefix ahead of any value. 8 tests. STILL OPEN, and it is the half that matters for acceptance: there is NO SERVER-SIDE REFUSAL yet. Fencing is a mitigation — it makes injection harder and does not make it impossible — whereas the PRD requires that "refused" means the server refuses. The refusal belongs at the two places untrusted text reaches an agent that can act: the compliance correction loop (page text becomes a user-role prompt to a child process with shell access) and the Share-to-CMS gate. Acceptance runbook not written.

subtasks.text: Snapshot validated and untrusted text fenced; the server-side refusal and the runbook are outstanding

tasks.title: Spending limits enforced
tasks.note: DEFERRED 2026-09-23, pending an answer from the owner. No spend cap exists. The PRD gives E4 no requirement number, no acceptance criterion and no phase — it says only that no cap exists and that this has been an accepted omission. Building one means inventing the limit, its scope and its behaviour, so three questions have been sent: what the limit is and per what; what happens when it is reached; and who may raise it. Nothing is built until those are answered.

subtasks.text: Deferred — the requirements document defines no spend cap to build against

tasks.title: CSRF and secure-cookie behaviour
tasks.note: NOTE CORRECTED 2026-09-23 — "no control" was false for the CMS and true for the console. Instatic already refused cross-origin state changes on every mutating surface and set correct cookie flags. The OPERATOR CONSOLE had no server-side origin check at all: astro.config.mjs set checkOrigin:false because Astro compares Origin against the request Host and the gateway rewrites Host, so every funnel POST was rejected. The defence was left to SameSite=Strict, which on this deployment protects nothing: the console, the CMS and the studio are served from ONE origin, so a script on any tenant page is same-origin with the console, and Path=/operator limits which requests carry the cookie, not which pages may send them. Exposed handlers included act-as, remove and expose. FIXED: a middleware gate comparing against the CONFIGURED origin (the same approach Instatic uses), with Sec-Fetch-Site consulted first and unknown configuration refusing; the unused state-changing GET /logout removed. 13-check self-test added. STILL OPEN: the CMS-side tests all run UNAUTHENTICATED, so none yet satisfies the PRD's "re-tested with valid credentials"; and originAllowed returns true when Origin is absent. Acceptance runbook not written.

subtasks.text: Console gate built + self-test; credentialed CMS tests and the no-Origin case outstanding

tasks.title: Unsafe HTML and script input neutralised
tasks.note: NOTE CORRECTED 2026-09-23 — "no test and no control" was false. Sanitisation is layered and already tested: write-time on every persisted tree (validate.ts), render-time dispatched on the DECLARED schema type with escape-by-default for anything unknown (escapeProps.ts), SVG bytes on upload and import, and inert Content-Disposition on served uploads. ONE REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: sanitizeRichtext FAILED OPEN — with no DOMPurify runtime it returned regex-stripped text that reads as clean, while its sibling sanitizeSvg twelve lines below refused. escapeProps passes richtext through UNESCAPED on the strength of that answer. Not theoretical: the runtime is module-level state set by a boot side effect, and this deployment runs from a network drive where Bun has been observed loading a module twice. It now refuses, and the CMS will not start without a working sanitiser. The test that pinned the old behaviour was inverted. STILL OPEN: no end-to-end test walks a hostile string from an anonymous ingress through to served bytes. Acceptance runbook not written.

subtasks.text: Fail-open fixed + boot assertion; end-to-end chain test and runbook outstanding

tasks.title: Audit-record tampering prevented
tasks.note: Covered by AC-B9.4; the approval store and the receipt store are both append-only by their own triggers. GAP FOUND 2026-09-23: listReceipts had ZERO callers anywhere, so there was no way to read a receipt outside psql — a validator could not even name one to attempt tampering with it. A read-only GET /api/tenants/<slug>/receipts route now exists (no edit or delete route, deliberately: immutability is the store's job, not the absence of a route). STILL OPEN: nothing exercises the triggers. There is no DB-backed test in the repo, and all 72 relay tests use an in-memory store, so the relay's append-only SQL has never been run. Both need a live database and must FAIL rather than skip when one is absent.

subtasks.text: Append-only by trigger; reader routed; trigger tests against a real database outstanding

tasks.title: Failed deployment and rollback exercised
tasks.note: BUILT 2026-09-23, with a correction to the earlier plan: wiring listKnownGood to restoreSiteBackup is not possible — one returns a directory of baked HTML for the CDN, the other takes a database client and a JSON row-dump for the CMS. A rollback is a RE-DEPLOY of retained bytes. A REAL DEFECT WAS FOUND FIRST: a bundle that FAILED verification was still filed as known-good, because retain ran above the line computing whether the site was live — with three generations kept, three bad deploys evicted every good one, so the ring a rollback reads from could be emptied by exactly the failure it exists to recover from. Only a verified bundle is now retained (unverified does not qualify: the check could not run). A failed deploy also wrote NO receipt at all — the one event this class exists to exercise left nothing in the append-only store; it does now. Added: rollbackTenant (listKnownGood's first caller ever), POST /rollback and GET /known-good, two receipt columns (kind, restored_from_receipt_id) since the PRD names a "rollback receipt" and defines no fields for one, and an 18-check self-test. NOT blocked by the relay: the GO gate is in the Connector, not the CMS publish path. STILL OPEN: acceptance runbook; and the CMS database still holds the content that was published, so a rollback restores what the SITE SERVES, not what the next publish would push — that is the R15 gap (restoreSiteBackup has no caller).

subtasks.text: Rollback, receipts and the known-good ring built + tested; acceptance runbook outstanding
